newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Chernogorneft says no 1996 dividend.
newsitem.headline: Russia Chernogorneft says no 1996 dividend.

text.p: Russian oil company Chernogorneft said on Thursday shareholders had voted against paying dividends on 1996 results at their annual shareholders meeting earlier this month.
"Despite undistributed profits in 1996 of 54 billion roubles, the decision was taken not to pay dividends," the company said in a statement. Chernogorneft did not pay dividends in 1995.
Financial figures for 1996 released by Chernogorneft on Thursday follow:
NOTES -- Figures for 1996 calculated to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis, figures for 1995 calculated on a cash basis.

Chernogorneft earlier reported 1996 pre-tax profits were $60.9 million to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis. Net profits were $42.2 million on an accruals basis, up from $35.3 million in 1995 on a cash basis.
According to figures audited by Ernst and Young to U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), Chernogorneft had net profit of 582.3 billion roubles in 1995.
The company statement said Chernogorneft plans to raise oil production by 1.7 percent in 1997.
It said the president of oil holding company SIDANKO, which owns 51 percent of Chernogorneft voting shares, was likely to appoint a general manager to run the company directly.

Russian accounting standards differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
